pr.title: Reach a relay location through a transport, and move the Git code behind GitTransport
pr.head: bfa35d893216c5f3c824c9492264dc26ae8f2613

summary: The relay carries encrypted agent presence, messages, and repository inbox records between machines. Its job currently reads and writes those records through Git commands. This layer introduces a store interface so an S3 implementation can share the existing delivery and outbox rules.

GitTransport keeps the current Git behavior. The job asks it to list versions, check a record before reading, read its bytes, and apply queued changes under their expected versions. S3 requests, configuration, and credentials belong to later layers.

cards.title: Terms used here
cards.html:
• Transport: the store-specific operations a relay job calls.
  • Version: a Git commit here; a queued change expects this version before replacing or deleting a record.
  • Outbox: the local queue of sealed records and deletions waiting to reach the store.

groups.title: Keep store operations behind one interface
groups.kicker: The job retains delivery and queue bookkeeping.
intro: A relay job must preserve the same sealing, limits, and concurrent-update rules regardless of its store. Transport describes that boundary, and GitTransport implements it using the existing Git commands.

The separate check operation rejects an invalid tree or oversized record before a read uses an opening slot. Applying changes returns an outcome for each record, including its landed version and whether its expected-version check failed. The job uses those outcomes to settle the outbox and update its cache.

files.note: Move Git operations into a transport and route the job through its four operations.

checks.text: Compared the moved fetch, tree check, blob read, leased push, and tracking-ref commands with the base, and traced every changed caller.
Seventeen focused tests passed for Git exchange, push races and partial lease failures, timeout recovery, bare clones, pre-read rejection limits, state merging, and per-record failures.
Job.open remains a Git-blob reader for existing callers in the tests; production examination uses transport reads followed by unseal.

groups.title: Record the boundary chosen during implementation
intro: The plan moves from ready to in progress and records why checking and reading are separate operations. It also assigns tracking-ref updates to the Git transport so the job can keep its store-independent bookkeeping.

files.note: Start implementation and append the four-operation transport and tracking-ref decisions.

checks.text: Read the plan against the implemented boundary. Hosted service and instance or container credentials remain explicitly deferred.
